fields.meta_title: Portfolio Landing Page Builder for Your Work | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a portfolio landing page from a prompt. See four examples: photo galleries, an NDA case study, art commissions, and code projects.
fields.h1: Build a Portfolio Landing Page That Puts Your Best Work First
fields.hero_description: Get a portfolio landing page built from one prompt, with your work up front and every inquiry saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Around Your Work
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page, the contact form under it, and the table that keeps every person who writes to you.
fields.feature_1:
Sections written from one sentence

Describe your work and who should see it, and Emergent builds the page: the intro, the project sections, and the contact form. Swap a project later with another prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every inquiry kept in your own table

The app saves each message from the contact form to a database you own, with the name, the email, and the project asked about. Sort the rows to see which project gets asked about.
fields.feature_3:
An alert when someone wants to hire you

Name the requests that matter in your prompt, such as a booking date or a licensing question, and the app sends an email, Slack, or in-app alert with the answers in it.
fields.feature_4:
Projects synced from the tools you use

The app connects to any tool with an API. Project lists can sync in from where the work lives, and new inquiries can sync out to your CRM without anyone copying them by hand.
fields.feature_5:
Your name as the address

Publish the page on a custom domain such as yourname.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. A short address fits on a resume or a business card.
fields.feature_6:
Free to start, yours to keep

The free tier covers building and publishing the page. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, so a developer can keep editing it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
38 of September's 64 inquiries came from weddings

Corin Sorrell shoots weddings, elopements, and portraits, and her page has three galleries, each with an inquiry form under it. Every inquiry is saved with the gallery the visitor was viewing. Of September's 64 inquiries, 38 came from the wedding gallery, 17 from elopements, and 9 from portraits.
fields.tab_content_2:
The NDA case study opens for any work email

The checkout redesign Maren Kaminski led is under NDA. Her page shows the project title and her role, and the full case study opens after a visitor enters a work email. Each visit is saved as a row with the email and the company, and Maren gets an email alert. In October, 23 visitors from 17 companies opened it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Commercial licensing requests reach her agent on Slack

Ines Ravel's commission form asks first how the art will be used: personal, editorial, or commercial. A commercial licensing request goes to her agent, Arlo Delvaux, as a Slack message with the brief and the budget. Last quarter, 14 of 52 requests were commercial; the other 38 stayed in her own queue.
fields.tab_content_4:
A project made public Tuesday has its card by Wednesday

Every night the app reads Theo Rosales's public projects through GitHub's API and builds a card for each with its language and a demo link. The page shows 9 cards. The newest is ledger-lite: Theo made it public on Tuesday, and its card was up by Wednesday morning.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Portfolio Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a portfolio landing page from one chosen action to a tested page with fast images and inquiries that reach you.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action a visitor takes
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write alt text for every image
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a visitor should do after looking at the work: ask about a date or request a license. Put that action under the work it belongs to, and leave everything else off the page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Show four to six projects, and lead with the one closest to the work you want next. Give each a title and your role, plus one result in plain numbers. Cut anything you would not take on again.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the sections, the fields on the form, and what should happen to each message: who hears about it and which table keeps it. Emergent builds the page and its database from that prompt, and another prompt changes either one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under WCAG 2.2, all non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Describe what each image shows, such as a checkout screen on a phone, never the file name.
fields.howto_step_5_des: The web.dev guide to LCP says sites should strive to have Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less. Resize each photo to the width it is shown at before you upload it, then load the page on a phone over cellular data.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit the form from your own phone once for each gallery or project. Check that every row lands in the table with the right project name, and that the alert reaches you before the address goes anywhere public.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the address where people look
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the page's address to your resume and your email signature. Once a month, read which project the inquiries named, and move that project to the top of the page.

faq_plan.q: What is a portfolio landing page?
faq_plan.a: A portfolio landing page is one page that shows a short selection of your best work and asks the visitor to take a single next step. That step might be asking about a date or opening a case study. A full portfolio site spreads the work over many pages; this page keeps the work and the one action together.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a portfolio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt that names your projects and where each inquiry should go, and Emergent's AI landing page builder builds the page and the database behind it. Change a section later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What do strong landing page portfolio examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: They lead with the work, before any introduction. Each project names the person's role and one result. Look for one clear action placed under the work it relates to, and a short list of projects rather than everything ever made. Borrow the structure of the examples you like, then fill it with your own work.

faq_plan.q: Should a portfolio landing page for company clients differ from one for individuals?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Expect a company client to forward the page to colleagues. Name the business problem each project solved, and add a way to reach you that does not need a phone call. If the page has to sell a service to a buying team rather than show your work, a b2b landing page fits that job better.

faq_plan.q: How do I show client work under NDA on a portfolio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask the client first what you may show, and get the answer in writing. If the full case study cannot be public, show the project title and your role, and open the details only to a visitor who enters a work email. The app saves each of those visits as a row with the company name.

faq_plan.q: Should a portfolio landing page use an inquiry form or an email address?
faq_plan.a: Use a form when you need the same facts from everyone, such as a date or a budget. A bare email address leaves you to ask for those facts one reply at a time. An app Emergent builds saves each form entry to a database you own, and you can name the requests that should send you an alert.

faq_plan.q: Can a printed business card link to my portfolio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Print a QR code on the card that opens the page, and give it a link tagged for print so you can tell those visits from the rest. Test the code on two phones before the print run. A qr code landing page covers how to set up a page whose visitors arrive from a scan.

faq_plan.q: Is a web address at my name worth it for a portfolio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes: a short address such as yourname.com is easier to type from a resume and reads as yours. Emergent includes custom domains, which use credits, and the page can sit at your name from the day it goes up.

faq_plan.q: Can a developer's portfolio landing page add new projects on its own?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the page reads your projects from the code host instead of from text you type. An app Emergent builds can pull data in from a service with an API on a schedule. Each new public project then gets its card without an edit to the page.

faq_plan.q: Can a portfolio landing page be the first step of a sales funnel?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The portfolio earns the inquiry, and the steps after it, such as a discovery call booking or a proposal, can live on their own pages. If you sell a fixed package rather than custom work, a sales funnel landing page is built around that sequence of steps.

This page shows four one-page portfolios for individual people (not studios), each built from a prompt, and follows the visitor after they look at the work: a wedding photographer's galleries that tag each inquiry with the gallery it came from, a UX designer's NDA case study that opens for a work email, an illustrator's commission form that sends commercial licensing requests to her agent, and a developer's project cards read from his public GitHub repositories. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, examples, what a one-page portfolio holds, how many projects to show, image alt text, load speed, a printed QR code, and own domain and code.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Portfolio Landing Page That Puts Your Best Work First', meta title 'Portfolio Landing Page Builder for Your Work | Emergent' and hero 'Get a portfolio landing page built from one prompt, with your work up front and every inquiry saved to a database you own.' cover the whole job; how-to description is one sentence under 140 characters.

intent.evidence: Informational SERP with image pack: definition in FAQ 1, four worked examples (photographer, UX designer under NDA, illustrator, developer), a seven-step how-to and a comparison table.

specificity.evidence: Speaks to individual portfolio owners: 'Of September's 64 inquiries, 38 came from the wedding gallery', 'The checkout redesign Maren Kaminski led is under NDA', 'Give each a title and your role, plus one result in plain numbers.' Table generated from the library (Unbounce, Landingi, Wix, single-vendor entries).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Corin Sorrell shoots weddings, elopements, and portraits', 'Describe your work and who should see it', 'Decide what a visitor should do after looking at the work'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q6/Q7 clean; one ', so' ending in feature_6; sentences carry one idea each ('The page shows 9 cards.').

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous details: 'ledger-lite: Theo made it public on Tuesday, and its card was up by Wednesday morning', 'Last quarter, 14 of 52 requests were commercial'. Notes recorded on feature templating and 'rather than'.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, api-connect, custom-domain, code-export, free-start). Third-party facts quoted from domain_sources: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 span verbatim, web.dev LCP 'sites should strive to have Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less' verbatim, GitHub API 'Lists public repositories for the specified user' supports tab 4. Numbers agree: 38+17+9=64; 14+38=52.

distinct.evidence: Tabs are individual portfolios (photo galleries, NDA case study, licensing commissions, GitHub cards), distinct from design-agency (studio budgets, sprints, pitch pages) and artist (musician signups, tour dates). D2 19% vs artist, under 30%; feature-grid templating noted.
